claims.band: The real time for a spike to settle back falls inside the published range 80 percent of the time, give or take 5 points.
claims.median: The middle figure beats the stock's own plain middle settling time by at least 20 percent in average error.

explanation.body: Its forecast takes this form: timing and distribution, over normalisation within up to 63 sessions (censor). It is graded on a loss score on each of its stated percentile lines, where lower is better. It would be ended if after 200 matured forecasts, coverage error exceeds 10 points or MAE does not beat the baseline. It counts as proven at 200 matured forecasts.
explanation.summary: When a stock's recent moves suddenly get much bigger than that stock's own usual moves, say how many trading days it is likely to take for its moves to settle back to its own usual size.

history.label: History, not live forecasts
history.note: Worked out spike by spike over the price history on record: each spike's forecast was built only from earlier spikes whose settling times were already known by then, then checked against what actually happened. Spikes that had not settled within 63 trading days count in the coverage figure exactly as the rules on this page state. The average-error figures run only over spikes that settled and had their own plain figure to compare with. These are study figures from the past, not the live record.

study_record.note: The earlier studies this clock is built from found that how much prices have been moving is the strongest guide to how much they will move next, and that a name's snap-back after a shock scales with how jagged that name usually is. Those are the studies' results, from their own longer histories. They are the reason this clock exists; they are not this clock's results.

kill_criterion: This tool is retired if, after 200 of its forecasts have matured, the share of real settling times that fell inside the published range is off by more than 10 points from the promised 80 percent, or its middle figure's average error is no better than the stock's own plain middle settling time.

live.correction_note: An earlier set of forecasts, made with a different way of measuring movement, was struck from the record and replaced by the forecasts above. The struck forecasts do not count in this record.

thin_cell_rule: Any graded group with fewer than 30 graded cases shows its count only, with no percentage and no error figure.
window_note: The original design judges each stock against three years of its own past. Only about nineteen months of daily history is on record here, so this clock judges each stock against all of its own past that exists, once at least six months of its own readings exist. Stocks without six months of readings are left out and counted.
